newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait seeks improved ties with Iraq's old friends.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait seeks improved ties with Iraq's old friends.

text.p: Kuwait said on Wednesday it was willing to improve ties with countries that sympathised with Iraq during its 1990-91 occupation of the Gulf Arab state.
Kuwait was angry with Jordan, Sudan, Yemen, Mauritania and the Palestinian Liberation Organisation over what it saw as sympathy with its former occupier.
"The state of Kuwait will not be captive to rigid positions without responding to developments," Planning Minister Ali al-Zmei'a told a news conference.

"It will work on amending the course of ties with the states with which ties have been blemished by...the traitorous Iraqi aggression," Zmei'a said in discussing the government's agenda until the year 2000.
"Reacting to any change would be through the commitment of the other sides to the (U.N.) Security Council resolutions," he said.

Kuwait has dropped its insistence that states apologise for backing Baghdad but wants them to help in freeing some 600 Kuwaitis its says are held by Iraq, condemn the occupation and help force Iraq to implement U.N. Security Council resolutions from the Gulf crisis.
